Or «ما» is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), in the position of a nominative, a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause «يدعون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ما».

muyesser-irab:58-58.t:
﴿سلام﴾: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "it is peace" (هو سلام).
﴿قولا﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) with fatḥa, of an omitted verb; together with its governor it is a naʿt (adjective) of «سلام», i.e. "peace, it being said to them as a saying" (سلام يقال لهم قولا).
﴿من رب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt of «قولًا».
﴿رحيم﴾: a naʿt of «رب».
Or:
﴿سلام﴾: a mubtadaʾ.
﴿قولا﴾: a mafʿūl muṭlaq; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the content of the clause, its governor being implied (muqaddar), and together with its governor it is a parenthetical clause.
﴿من رب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ «سلام».
﴿رحيم﴾: a naʿt of «رب».
The nominal clause is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), so it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:59-59.t: ﴿وامتازوا اليوم أيها المجرمون﴾: the clause is the object of an omitted verb of saying (maqūl li-qawl maḥdhūf), i.e. "and Allah will say to them" (ويقول لهم الله); «امتازوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «امتازوا»; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), with the vocative particle omitted; «ها» is for drawing attention; and «المجرمون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أي».

muyesser-irab:60-60.t:
﴿ألم أعهد إليكم يا بني آدم﴾: a clause strung in the series of what is said to them; the hamza is for a question that includes these meanings; «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; «أعهد» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "I" (أنا); «إليكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعهد»; «يا» is a vocative particle; «بني» is the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf; and «آدم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿أن لا تعبدوا الشيطان﴾: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya). «لا» is prohibitive. «تعبدوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive «لا», and the wāw is the fāʿil. «الشيطان» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Or «أن» is maṣdariyya, and it together with what it governs is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, i.e. "did I not enjoin upon you the abandoning of the worship of Satan" (ألم أعهد إليكم بترك عبادة الشيطان); the clause «لا تعبدوا الشيطان» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdariyya «أن», with no grammatical position.
﴿إنه لكم عدو مبين﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the hāʾ is its noun, «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «عدوّ», or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); «عدو» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and «مبين» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for the prohibition, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:61-61.t: ﴿وأن اعبدوني هذا صراط مستقيم﴾: «أن اعبدوني» is conjoined to «أن لا تعبدوا»; «اعبدوني» is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «صراط» is the khabar (predicate), and «مستقيم» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for the command.

muyesser-irab:62-62.t:
﴿ولقد أضل منكم جبلا كثيرا﴾: speech that is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the lām is in answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «أضل» is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); «منكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أضل»; «جبلًّا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «كثيرًا» is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿أفلم تكونوا تعقلون﴾: the hamza is for the rhetorical question of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive, «تكونوا» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the wāw is its noun, and the clause «تعقلون» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:63-63.t: ﴿هذه جهنم التي كنتم توعدون﴾: speech that is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «هذه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «جهنم» is the khabar (predicate), «التي» is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The tāʾ is the noun of «كان», and the clause «توعدون» is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:64-64.t: ﴿اصلوها اليوم بما كنتم تكفرون﴾: «اصلوها» is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصلوها»; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اصلوها», the bāʾ being causal and «ما» maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of your disbelief" (بسبب كفركم); «كنتم»: «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause «تكفرون» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «كنتم تكفرون» has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:65-65.t:
﴿اليوم نختم على أفواههم﴾: «اليوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نختم»; «نختم» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); «على أفواههم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نختم».
﴿وتكلمنا أيديهم وتشهد أرجلهم بما كانوا يكسبون﴾: «تكلمنا» is an imperfect verb, «نا» is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «أيديهم» is a delayed fāʿil; «تشهد أرجلهم» is conjoined to «تكلمنا أيديهم»; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تكلمنا», «ما» being maṣdariyya or a relative; «كانوا»: «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause «يكسبون» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:66-66.t:
﴿ولو نشاء لطمسنا على أعينهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «لو» is conditional, «نشاء» is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "if We willed their effacement" (لو نشاء طمسها); the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو», and the clause «طمسنا» has no grammatical position: it is a past verb, «نا» being the fāʿil; «على أعينهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «طمسنا».
﴿فاستبقوا الصراط﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «استبقوا» is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to «لطمسنا»; «الصراط» is accusative (manṣūb) by removal of the preposition, the original being "and they would race to the path" (فاستبقوا إلى الصراط); or it is the mafʿūl bihi, «فاستبقوا» being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of "they hastened towards" (ابتدروا).
﴿فأنى يبصرون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «أنى» is an interrogative noun meaning "how" (كيف), in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); «يبصرون» is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the question here means negation, i.e. "they would not see" (لا يبصرون).

muyesser-irab:67-67.t:
﴿ولو نشاء لمسخناهم على مكانتهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «لو» is conditional, «نشاء» is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); the object of «نشاء» is omitted, i.e. "if We willed their transformation" (لو نشاء مسخهم); the lām occurs in the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو», and the clause «مسخناهم» has no grammatical position: it is a past verb, «نا» is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «على مكانتهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We would have transformed them in their state" (لمسخناهم على حالتهم).
﴿فما استطاعوا مضيا ولا يرجعون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «ما» is negating, «استطاعوا» is a verb and its fāʿil, «مضيًّا» is the mafʿūl bihi, and «لا يرجعون» is conjoined.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t: ﴿ومن نعمره ننكسه في الخلق أفلا يعقلون﴾: speech that is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «مَن» is a conditional noun that makes jussive; «نعمره» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «ننكسه» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "we" (نحن), and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «في الخلق» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ننكسه», or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the hamza is for the rhetorical question of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted that the context requires, «لا» is negating, and «يعقلون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:69-69.t:
﴿وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له﴾: speech that is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «ما» is negating; «علمناه» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «الشعر» is a second mafʿūl bihi; «ما» is conjoined [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. the wāw conjoins and «ما» is negating]; «ينبغي» is an imperfect verb conjoined to «علمناه»; and «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينبغي».
﴿إن هو إلا ذكر وقرآن مبين﴾: «إن» is negating, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), «ذكر» is the khabar (predicate), «قرآن» is conjoined to «ذكر», and «مبين» is a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:70-70.t: ﴿لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين﴾: the lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); «ينذر» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted indicated by the context of the speech, i.e. "He sent it down to him so that he may warn" (أنزل عليه لينذر); «مَن» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «كان» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The noun of «كان» is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو), and «حيًّا» is its khabar (predicate); «يحق» is conjoined to «لينذر»; «القول» is the fāʿil (agent); and «على الكافرين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يحق».

muyesser-irab:71-71.t:
﴿أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما﴾: the hamza is for the question of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), its original being «وألم يروا», the interrogative being placed first because it takes the lead (al-ṣadāra); or the wāw conjoins to something omitted that the context requires, the implied form being "did they not reflect and did they not see" (ألم يتفكروا ولم يروا); «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; «يروا» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the seeing being cognitive (ʿilmiyya); «أنا»: «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «نا» is its noun, and the clause «خلقنا» is its khabar (predicate), being a verb and its fāʿil; «أن» and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of «يروا»; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقنا», i.e. "for their sake and their benefit" (لأجلهم وانتفاعهم); «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «عملت» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. «عملته»; «أيدينا» is the fāʿil; and «أنعامًا» is the object of «خلقنا».
﴿فهم لها مالكون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «لها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مالكون», and «مالكون» is the khabar of «هم».

muyesser-irab:72-72.t: ﴿وذللناها لهم فمنها ركوبهم ومنها يأكلون﴾: «ذللناها» is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ذللناها»; the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); «منها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); «ركوبهم» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); «منها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يأكلون»; and «يأكلون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:73-73.t:
﴿ولهم فيها منافع ومشارب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), «منافع» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مشارب» is conjoined to «منافع».
﴿أفلا يشكرون﴾: the hamza is for the rhetorical question of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), the fāʾ is a conjunction, «لا» is negating, and «يشكرون» is an imperfect verb, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:74-74.t:
﴿واتخذوا من دون الله آلهة﴾: the wāw conjoins to something implied that the context calls for, i.e. "they did not give thanks" (ما فعلوا الشكر); «اتخذوا» is an imperative verb [Translator's note: so in the source; «اتخذوا» here is a past verb] and its fāʿil (agent); «من دون الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object of «اتخذوا»; and «آلهة» is its first object.
﴿لعلهم ينصرون﴾: «لعل» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «هم» is its noun, and the clause «ينصرون» is its khabar (predicate), the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause of hope is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. "in the state of their hoping for help from their gods" (حال كونهم راجين النصر من آلهتهم).

muyesser-irab:75-75.t: ﴿لا يستطيعون نصرهم وهم لهم جند محضرون﴾: «لا» is negating, «يستطيعون» is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and «نصرهم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جند»; «جند» is the khabar (predicate) of «هم»; and «محضرون» is a second khabar of «هم», or a naʿt (adjective) of «جند».

muyesser-irab:76-76.t: ﴿فلا يحزنك قولهم إنا نعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); «لا» is prohibitive; «يحزنك» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لا», and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «قولهم» is the fāʿil (agent); «إنا»: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «نا» is its noun, and the clause «نعلم» is its khabar (predicate), its fāʿil being latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); «ما» is a relative, the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "that which they conceal" (الذي يسرونه), or maṣdariyya, i.e. "their concealing" (إسرارهم); the clause «يسرون» has no grammatical position; and «ما يعلنون» is conjoined to «ما يسرون».

muyesser-irab:77-77.t: ﴿أولم ير الإنسان أنا خلقناه من نطفة فإذا هو خصيم مبين﴾: speech that is resumptive, with no grammatical position; the hamza is for a question of disapproval and wonder (istifhām inkārī taʿajjubī), and the wāw is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; «ير» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; «الإنسان» is the fāʿil (agent); «أنا»: «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), «نا» is its noun, and the clause «خلقناه» is its khabar (predicate); «أن» and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of «ير»; «خلقناه» is a verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من نطفة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خلقناه»; the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «خصيم» is the khabar; and «مبين» is a naʿt (adjective). The clause «إذا هو خصيم مبين» is conjoined to the clause «لم ير الإنسان», falling with it within the scope of the disapproval and wonder.

muyesser-irab:78-78.t:
﴿وضرب لنا مثلا ونسي خلقه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «ضرب» is a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); «لنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ضرب»; «مثلًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «نسي» is conjoined to «ضرب»; and «خلقه» is the mafʿūl bihi; or the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), with «قد» implied, i.e. "while he had forgotten his own creation" (وقد نسي خلقه).
﴿قال من يحي العظام وهي رميم﴾: «مَن» is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يحيي العظام» is the khabar (predicate); the wāw is circumstantial, «هي» is a mubtadaʾ, «رميم» is the khabar, and the clause is in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:79-79.t:
﴿قل يحييها الذي أنشأها أول مرة﴾: «يحييها» is an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «يحييها» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); «الذي» is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause «أنشأها» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «أول مرة» is accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنشأها».
﴿وهو بكل خلق عليم﴾: the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «بكل» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «عليم»; «عليم» is the khabar (predicate) of «هو»; the clause «وهو بكل...» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:80-80.t:
﴿الذي جعل لكم من الشجر الأخضر نارا﴾: «الذي» is a badal (substitute) from the «الذي» mentioned just before, and the clause «جعل» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object; «من الشجر الأخضر» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and «نارًا» is the first object of «جعل».
﴿فإذا أنتم منه توقدون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «منه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «توقدون», and the clause «توقدون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أنتم».

muyesser-irab:81-81.t:
﴿أوليس الذي خلق السماوات والأرض بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم﴾: the hamza is for the rhetorical question of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw conjoins to something implied that the situation requires; «ليس» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb; «الذي» is its noun, and the clause «خلق...» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and «قادر» is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar (predicate) of «ليس»; «على» is a preposition, and «أن» with what falls within its scope is in the position of a genitive by «على», the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادر»; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); and «مثلهم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بلى﴾: a particle of answer for cancelling the negation, i.e. "yes, He is able to do that" (بلى هو قادر على ذلك).
﴿وهو الخلاق العليم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «الخلاق» is the khabar, and «العليم» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:82-82.t: ﴿إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون﴾: «إنما» is a restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa) [particle]; «أمره» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «إذا» is an adverb of the future, and the clause «أراد» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to it, being a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); «شيئًا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «أن» is maṣdariyya, and «يقول» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن»; «أن» and what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «أمره»; «له» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقول»; the clause «كن» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl): it is a complete (tāmm) imperative verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the fāʾ is a conjunction; «يكون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil being latent, and the verb with its fāʿil is a clause in the position of a nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the clause being conjoined to «أمره».

muyesser-irab:83-83.t:
﴿فسبحان الذي بيده ملكوت كل شيء﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); «سبحان» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb; «الذي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «بيده» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); «ملكوت كل شيء» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause «بيده ملكوت كل شيء» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿وإليه ترجعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «إليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ترجعون», and «ترجعون» is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يس﴾: the discussion of the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has already been given at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿والقرآن الحكيم﴾: الواو: a particle of oath and of the genitive; القرآن: that by which the oath is sworn (muqsam bihi), a noun in the genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); الحكيم: naʿt (adjective), genitive.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إنك لمن المرسلين﴾: إنك: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the kāf is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); من المرسلين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿على صراط مستقيم﴾: على صراط: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾, or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun of inna or from the pronoun latent (mustakinn) in its khabar, or attached to ﴿المرسلين﴾; مستقيم: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿صراط﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿تنزيل العزيز الرحيم﴾: تنزيلَ: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "Allah has sent that down, a sending down of the Mighty, the Merciful", or accusative for praise (manṣūb ʿalā al-madḥ) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "أعني" (I mean) or "أمدح" (I praise); العزيز: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الرحيم: naʿt (adjective), genitive.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم﴾: the lām: for cause (taʿlīl); تنذر: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb is genitive by the lām, and the lām of cause with its genitive is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنزيل﴾, or to the sense of His words ﴿من المرسلين﴾, i.e. "you are sent so that you may warn". قومًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ما: negating; أُنذر: a passive past verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); آباؤهم: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the attached pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿ما أنذر آباؤهم﴾ is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قومًا﴾. Or ﴿ما﴾ in His words ﴿ما أنذر آباؤهم﴾ is a relative in the position of accusative as the second object of ﴿تنذر﴾, and the clause ﴿أُنذِر آباؤهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position, i.e. "that you may warn a people of that of which their fathers were warned"; or ﴿ما﴾ is a qualified indefinite (nakira mawṣūfa) in the position of accusative as a second object, and the clause ﴿أُنذِر آباؤهم﴾ is a naʿt of ﴿ما﴾, i.e. "that you may warn a people of a punishment of which their fathers were warned"; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, i.e. "that you may warn a people with the warning of their fathers".
﴿فهم غافلون﴾: الفاء: causal (taʿlīliyya), giving the reason for the negation if ﴿ما﴾ is taken as negating, i.e. "they were not warned, so because of that they are heedless"; or giving the reason for his warning, upon him be blessing and peace, or for his being sent, namely their heedlessness, which made it necessary; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); غافلون: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t: ﴿لقد حق القول على أكثرهم فهم لا يؤمنون﴾: لقد: the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath, and ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); حق: a past verb; القول: fāʿil (agent); على أكثرهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حق﴾, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الفاء: causal (taʿlīliyya); هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); لا: negating; يؤمنون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿إنا جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; إنّا: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is the noun of inna; جعلنا: a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); في أعناقهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object of جعلنا; أغلالا: the first object of جعلنا; the clause ﴿جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿فهي إلى الأذقان﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); هي: a pronoun referring to the shackles, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); إلى الأذقان: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar, i.e. ﴿فهي واصلةٌ إلى الأذقان﴾ (and they reach up to the chins); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿جعلنا﴾.
﴿فهم مقمحون﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence; هم: mubtadaʾ; مقمحون: khabar; the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿هي إلى الأذقان﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وجعلنا من بين أيديهم سدا ومن خلفهم سدا﴾: الواو: conjunctive; جعلنا: a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); من بين: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object of جعلنا; أيديهم: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; سدًّا: the first object of جعلنا; ومن خلفهم سدًّا: conjoined to ﴿من بين أيديهم سدًّا﴾; the clause ﴿جعلنا من بين أيديهم...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿جعلنا في أعناقهم أغلالا...﴾.
﴿فأغشيناهم﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); أغشيناهم: a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the verbal clause is conjoined to the preceding clause ﴿جعلنا﴾.
﴿فهم لا يبصرون﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); لا: negating; يبصرون: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا يبصرون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿هم﴾, and the nominal clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿أغشيناهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وسواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أم لم تنذرهم لا يؤمنون﴾: الواو: resumptive, or conjunctive; سواء: a fronted khabar (predicate); عليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سواء﴾; ﴿أأنذرتهم﴾: the hamza is for equalisation (taswiya), and أنذرتهم is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hamza with the verb after it is to be construed as a maṣdar, a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "your warning them and its absence are the same". ﴿أم﴾: a conjunction corresponding to the hamza; ﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; ﴿تنذرهم﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "أنت", the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿لم تنذرهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أنذرتهم﴾; the clause ﴿لا يؤمنون﴾ is a resumption confirming what precedes it, with no grammatical position, or an emphasising ḥāl (circumstantial) for it, or a badal (substitute) from it; and the clause ﴿وسواء عليهم...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position, or conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب﴾: ﴿إنما﴾: restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿تنذر﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "أنت"; ﴿مَن﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿اتبع﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو"; ﴿الذكر﴾: the object of اتبع; the clause ﴿اتبع الذكر﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿خشي﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو"; ﴿الرحمن﴾: the object of خشي; the clause ﴿خشي الرحمن﴾ is conjoined to ﴿اتبع الذكر﴾; ﴿بالغيب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of خشي, i.e. "he feared the All-Merciful while absent from people's eyes in his private moments, or while absent from His punishment"; or the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the object of خشي, i.e. "he feared the punishment of the All-Merciful while the punishment is hidden from him".
﴿فبشره بمغفرة وأجر كريم﴾: ﴿فبشره﴾: the fāʾ is to make the glad tidings follow upon what precedes them, namely following the Reminder and fearing; ﴿بشره﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "أنت", and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بمغفرة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿بشره﴾; ﴿وأجر﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿أجر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿مغفرة﴾; ﴿كريم﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجر﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إنا نحن نحي الموتى ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم﴾: ﴿إنّا﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is the noun of inna; ﴿نحن﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); نحيي: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "نحن"; ﴿الموتى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿نحيي الموتى﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of نحن, and the nominal clause ﴿نحن نحيي الموتى﴾ is the khabar of inna; or ﴿نحن﴾ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and the verbal clause ﴿نحيي الموتى﴾ is the khabar of inna. ﴿ونكتب﴾: الواو: conjunctive, and نكتب: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "نحن"; ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; ﴿قدموا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿قدموا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿وآثارهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿آثارهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ما﴾, accusative; the clause ﴿ونكتب ما قدموا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿نحيي الموتى﴾.
﴿وكل شيء أحصيناه في إمام مبين﴾: الواو: conjunctive; ﴿كل﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative by an omitted verb indicated by what follows, its implied form being "أحصينا"; ﴿شيء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿أحصيناه﴾: a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أحصيناه﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya) with no grammatical position. ﴿في إمام﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أحصيناه﴾; ﴿مبين﴾: naʿt (adjective), genitive.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t: ﴿واضرب لهم مثلا أصحاب القرية إذ جاءها المرسلون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿اضرب﴾: an imperative verb in the sense of "make"; ﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اضرب﴾; ﴿مثلا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿اضرب﴾; ﴿أصحاب﴾: first mafʿūl bihi; or ﴿اضرب﴾ is in the sense of "mention", ﴿مثلا﴾ is mafʿūl bihi, and ﴿أصحاب﴾ is a badal (substitute) on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the example of the people"; ﴿القرية﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿إذ﴾: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from ﴿أصحاب القرية﴾; ﴿جاءها﴾: a past verb, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; ﴿المرسلون﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿جاءها المرسلون﴾ is in the position of genitive through the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿إذ أرسلنا إليهم اثنين﴾: ﴿إذ﴾: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from the ﴿إذ﴾ in the previous ayah; ﴿أرسلنا﴾: a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ﴿اثنين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أرسلنا﴾; the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾ is in the position of genitive by annexation.
﴿فكذبوهما﴾: ﴿فكذبوهما﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿كذبوهما﴾ is a past verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿كذبوهما﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أرسلنا﴾.
﴿فعززنا بثالث﴾: ﴿فعززنا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿عززنا﴾ is a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ the fāʿil; ﴿بثالث﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عززنا﴾; the clause ﴿عززنا﴾ is conjoined to the one before it.
﴿فقالوا إنا إليكم مرسلون﴾: ﴿فقالوا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ﴿قالوا﴾ is a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; ﴿إنا﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿إليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مرسلون﴾; ﴿مرسلون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ﴿إنا إليكم مرسلون﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿قالوا...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿عززنا﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿قالوا ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿ما﴾: negating; ﴿أنتم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); ﴿بشر﴾: the khabar (predicate) of أنتم; ﴿مثلنا﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بشر﴾, and the first-person plural pronoun ﴿نا﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿ما أنتم...﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of accusative.
﴿وما أنزل الرحمن من شيء﴾: ﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿أنزل﴾: a past verb; ﴿الرحمن﴾: fāʿil; ﴿من﴾: a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr ṣila); ﴿شيء﴾: genitive in form by ﴿من﴾, accusative in position as the object of أنزل; the clause ﴿ما أنزل﴾ is conjoined to the reported speech, in the position of accusative.
﴿إن أنتم إلا تكذبون﴾: ﴿إن﴾: negating; ﴿أنتم﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction; ﴿تكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿تكذبون﴾ is the khabar, and the clause ﴿إن أنتم إلا تكذبون﴾ is resumptive within the scope of the saying, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t: ﴿قالوا ربنا يعلم إنا إليكم لمرسلون﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿ربنا﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يعلم﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil of يعلم is latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; ﴿إنا﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; ﴿إليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مرسلون﴾; ﴿لمرسلون﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿مرسلون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ﴿إنا إليكم لمرسلون﴾ stands in place of the two objects of يعلم; the clause ﴿يعلم﴾ is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿ربنا يعلم...﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of accusative.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وما علينا إلا البلاغ المبين﴾: ﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿علينا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr); ﴿البلاغ﴾: a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿المبين﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿ربنا يعلم...﴾.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إنا﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; تطيرنا: a past verb and ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil; ﴿بكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تطيرنا﴾; the clause ﴿تطيرنا﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم﴾: ﴿لئن﴾: the lām is preparing for an oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam) and ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, of conversion (to the past) and of the jussive; ﴿تنتهوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; ﴿لنرجمنكم﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and ﴿نرجمنكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "نحن", the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿لنرجمنكم﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
﴿وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم﴾: ﴿وليمسنكم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿يمسنكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi and the mīm is the sign of the plural; ﴿منا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿عذاب﴾; ﴿عذاب﴾: fāʿil; ﴿أليم﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عذاب﴾; the clause ﴿ليمسنكم﴾ is conjoined to the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿قالوا طائركم معكم﴾: ﴿قالوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿طائركم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿معكم﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿طائركم معكم...﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿أئن ذكرتم﴾: ﴿أئن﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī) and ﴿إن﴾ is conditional; ﴿ذكرتم﴾: a passive past verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the implied form being "if you are reminded, do you take an evil omen, or threaten with stoning and torment?"; the conditional clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying, with no grammatical position.
﴿بل أنتم قوم مسرفون﴾: ﴿بل﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿أنتم﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿قوم﴾: khabar; ﴿مسرفون﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى﴾: ﴿وجاء﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or resumptive, and ﴿جاء﴾ is a past verb; ﴿من أقصى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جاء﴾; ﴿المدينة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿رجل﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of جاء; ﴿يسعى﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; the clause ﴿يسعى﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رجل﴾, and the clause ﴿وجاء من أقصى...﴾ is conjoined, or resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿قال يا قوم اتبعوا المرسلين﴾: ﴿قال﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو"; ﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle; ﴿قوم﴾: the one addressed (munādā), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa because it is annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; ﴿اتبعوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; ﴿المرسلين﴾: the object of اتبعوا; the vocative clause ﴿يا قوم...﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿اتبعوا المرسلين﴾ is the answer to the vocative.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿اتبعوا من لا يسألكم أجرا﴾: ﴿اتبعوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as the object of اتبعوا; ﴿لا﴾: negating; ﴿يسألكم﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "هو", the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the mīm is the sign of the plural; ﴿أجرًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿لا يسألكم أجرا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿اتبعوا من لا يسألكم﴾ is a badal (substitute) from the clause ﴿اتبعوا المرسلين﴾, or a tawkīd (emphasis).
﴿وهم مهتدون﴾: ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and ﴿هم﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿مهتدون﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿لا يسألكم أجرا﴾, with no grammatical position, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني﴾: ﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and it is a disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); ﴿لي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the interrogative ﴿ما﴾; ﴿لا﴾: negating; ﴿أعبد﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "أنا"; ﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as the object of أعبد; ﴿فطرني﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو", referring to the relative noun, and the yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿فطرني﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿لا أعبد...﴾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause ﴿ما لي لا أعبد...﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿اتبعوا﴾.
﴿وإليه ترجعون﴾: ﴿وإليه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿ترجعون﴾; ﴿ترجعون﴾: a passive imperfect verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the wāw of the plural is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿فطرني﴾, with no grammatical position, or circumstantial.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿أأتخذ من دونه آلهة﴾: ﴿أأتخذ﴾: the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī), or in the sense of negation; ﴿أتخذ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "أنا"; ﴿من دونه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿أتخذ﴾, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿آلهة﴾: first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿إن يردن الرحمن بضر لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا ولا ينقذون﴾: ﴿إن﴾: conditional; ﴿يردنِ﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) with sukūn; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ, omitted to follow the script of the Muṣḥaf, is mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الرحمن﴾: fāʿil; ﴿بضر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يردن﴾; ﴿لا﴾: negating, without governing effect; ﴿تغن﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿عني﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تغن﴾; ﴿شفاعتهم﴾: fāʿil, nominative, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿شيئًا﴾: standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or mafʿūl bihi; His words ﴿لا تغن عني شفاعتهم شيئا﴾ are the apodosis. ﴿ولا ينقذون﴾: conjoined to ﴿لا تغن﴾; ﴿ينقذون﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection, and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi; the conditional sentence is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿آلهة﴾, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t: ﴿إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين﴾: ﴿إني﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ of the speaker is its noun; ﴿إذًا﴾: a particle of response, without governing effect; ﴿لفي ضلال﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿في ضلال﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿مبين﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ضلال﴾; the clause is resumptive within the scope of the saying, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿إني آمنت بربكم فاسمعون﴾: ﴿إني﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ of the speaker is its noun; ﴿آمنت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿بربكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿آمنت﴾, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿آمنت بربكم﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿فاسمعونِ﴾: the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ), and ﴿اسمعون﴾ is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿اسمعون﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿آمنت﴾, and the clause ﴿إني آمنت...﴾ is resumptive within the scope of the saying, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿قيل ادخل الجنة﴾: ﴿قيل﴾: a passive past verb (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu); ﴿ادخل﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "أنت"; ﴿الجنة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ادخل الجنة﴾ is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the sentence is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿قال يا ليت قومي يعلمون﴾: ﴿قال﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, implied as "هو"; ﴿يا﴾: a particle of alerting (tanbīh), or a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted; ﴿ليت﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing wishing; ﴿قومي﴾: the noun of layta, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿يعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿يعلمون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of layta; the clause ﴿يا ليت قومي يعلمون﴾ is the reported speech, in the position of accusative, and the clause ﴿قال يا ليت...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿بما غفر لي ربي وجعلني من المكرمين﴾: ﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of genitive, i.e. "they would know of the sins that my Lord forgave me"; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾ and the verb ﴿غفر﴾ is genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "they would know of my Lord's forgiving me"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعلمون﴾. ﴿غفر﴾: a past verb. ﴿لي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿غفر﴾. ﴿ربي﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative with a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, and the yāʾ of the speaker is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿غفر لي ربي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. ﴿وجعلني﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿جعلني﴾ is a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "هو"; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من المكرمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿جعلني من المكرمين﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿غفر لي ربي﴾.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وما أنزلنا على قومه من بعده من جند من السماء﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; ﴿ما﴾: negating; ﴿أنزلنا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿عليهم﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah reads ﴿على قومه﴾.]: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلنا﴾; ﴿من بعده﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); من: a redundant preposition (ḥarf jarr ṣila); جند: genitive in form, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿من السماء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جند﴾.
﴿وما كنا منزلين﴾: الواو: conjunctive; ما: negating; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun; منزلين: its khabar (predicate).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Yā Sīn
Meccan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis that ﴿يس﴾ means: ”يا إنْسانُ“ ("O human being"); it has also come as: ”يا رَجُلُ“ ("O man"), and as: ”يا مُحَمَّدُ“ ("O Muḥammad"). What the experts in Arabic hold is that it is in the position of ”الـم“ — an opening of the sūra. It has also come that it means an oath. Some of them — I mean some of the Arabs — say: ”ياسِينَ والقُرْآنَ“, with fatḥa on the nūn; this is permissible in Arabic, but the sukūn is better, because these are letters of the alphabet, and we have explained the like of this. As for the one who gives it fatḥa, it is on two accounts: either ”يـس“ is a name of the sūra, quoted as is (ḥikāya), as though he said: "Recite Yā Sīn", and it is on the pattern of ”هابِيلَ“ and ”قابِيلَ“, a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf); or it may be that he gave it fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿والقُرْآنِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ ("by the wise Qurʾān"): its meaning is that its verses have been made firm, and in them have been made clear the command, the prohibition, the parables and the stories of the bygone nations.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿إنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ("you are indeed among the messengers"): this is an address to Muḥammad ﷺ, and it is the answer to the oath, the answer of ”والقُرْآنِ إنَّكَ لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ“.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ ("on a straight path"), that is: on the way of the prophets who preceded you. The best [analysis] in Arabic is that ”لَمِنَ المُرْسَلِينَ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“, and ”عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ“ a second khabar; so the meaning is: "you are indeed among the messengers who were sent upon a straight way".

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿تَنْـزِيلَ العَزِيزِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ ("a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful"). It is read ”تَنْزِيلُ“ with the nominative and [with] the accusative. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "Allah has sent that down as a sending-down"; and whoever reads it in the nominative takes it in the sense: "what has been sent down to you is a revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful".

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا ما أُنْذِرَ آباؤُهم فَهم غافِلُونَ﴾ ("that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless"). It has come in the exegesis: "that you may warn a people with the like of what their forefathers were warned with"; and it has come: "that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned", in which case ”ما“ is a negation. This — and Allah knows best — is the preferred view, because His saying ”فَهم غافِلُونَ“ is evidence for the meaning "their forefathers were not warned"; whereas if their forefathers had been warned [and yet] "they are heedless", there is something far-fetched in it — but it has come in the exegesis. The evidence for the negation is His saying: ﴿وَما آتَيْناهم مِن كُتُبٍ يَدْرُسُونَها وما أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ مِن نَذِيرٍ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 44]; had their forefathers been warned, they would have been warned and studying books — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿لَقَدْ حَقَّ القَوْلُ عَلى أكْثَرِهِمْ﴾ ("the word has indeed come true against most of them"). ”اَلْقَوْلُ“ here — and Allah knows best — is like His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. The meaning is: "the word has come true against most of them because of their disbelief and obstinacy; Allah led them astray and withheld them from guidance".

zajjaj:8-8.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا في أعْناقِهِمْ أغْلالا﴾ ("We have put shackles on their necks"). Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd — may Allah have mercy on them — read: ”إنّا جَعَلْنا في أيْمانِهِمْ“ ("on their right hands"), and some read: ”في أيْدِيهِمْ أغْلالًا“ ("on their hands"). Neither of these two readings should be recited, because they differ from the muṣḥaf. The meaning in His saying ”في أعْناقِهِمْ“, and [in the reading of] whoever read ”في أيْمانِهِمْ“, and whoever read ”في أيْدِيهِمْ“, is one and the same; that is because the shackle is not on the neck without the hand, nor on the hand without the neck. So the meaning is: "We have put shackles on their necks and on their right hands". ﴿فَهِيَ إلى الأذْقانِ﴾ ("and they reach to the chins") is an allusion (kināya) to the hands, not to the necks, because the shackle makes the hand adjoin the chin; the neck is already close to the chin — the shackle does not bring the neck to the chin.
And His saying: ﴿فَهم مُقْمَحُونَ﴾ ("so their heads are forced up"): ”اَلْمُقْمَحُ“ is the one who raises his head and lowers his gaze. The two months of Kānūn are called ”شَهْرا قِماحٍ“ ("the two months of head-raising"), because when the camels come to the water they raise their heads on account of its intense cold; hence "the two months of qimāḥ" is said. The necks were mentioned and the hands were not mentioned only for brevity and concision, because the shackle includes the neck and the hand; and whoever reads ”في أيْمانِهِمْ“ — that too indicates the neck. Similar to this is the saying of al-Muthaqqib:
؎فَما أدْرِي إذا يَمَّمْتُ أرْضًا ∗∗∗ أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِينِي؟
(I do not know, when I head for a land seeking good, which of the two will meet me:)
أألْخَيْرُ الَّذِي أنا أبْتَغِيهِ ... أمِ الشَّرُّ الَّذِي هو يَبْتَغِينِي
(the good that I am seeking, or the evil that is seeking me?)
He mentioned the good alone and then said ”أيُّهُما يَلِينِي“ ("which of the two will meet me"), because it is already known that good and evil are both laid before a person; he does not know, when he heads for a land, whether this or that will meet him. Similar to it in the Book of Allah is: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81] ("garments that protect you from the heat"), and He did not mention the cold, because what protects from this protects from that.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا﴾ ("and We have put before them a barrier"), and ”سُدًّا“ — with fatḥa and with ḍamma — and their meaning is one. It has been said: ”اَلسَّدُّ“ is the work of a human being, and ”اَلسُّدُّ“ is the natural form of what is blocked. There are two ways in it. One of them has come in the exegesis: some people intended harm to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah came between them and that, so they were made like one in this state: they were made like one whose right hand has been shackled, whose way has been blocked before him and behind him, and over whose sight a covering has been put — and that is the meaning of ﴿فَأغْشَيْناهُمْ﴾ ("and We have covered them"); it is also read ”فَأعْشَيْناهم“, with an undotted ʿayn ("We have dimmed their sight"). So Allah came between them and His Messenger; and among these was Abū Jahl, according to what is related. And it is possible that He is describing their being led astray, so He said: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا في أعْناقِهِمْ أغْلالا فَهي إلى الأذْقانِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 8], that is: We led them astray, and held back their hands from spending in the way of Allah and from striving in what brings one near to Allah; ﴿وَجَعَلْنا مِن بَيْنِ أيْدِيهِمْ سَدًّا ومِن خَلْفِهِمْ سَدًّا﴾, just as He said: ﴿خَتَمَ اللَّهُ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ وعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 7] — the verse. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿وَسَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أأنْذَرْتَهم أمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهم لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 10], because whoever Allah has led astray in this way, warning does not benefit him.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿إنَّما تُنْذِرُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ الذِّكْرَ﴾ ("you only warn the one who follows the Reminder"), that is: the one who listens to the Qurʾān and follows it. ﴿وَخَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالغَيْبِ﴾ ("and fears the Most Merciful unseen"), that is: fears Allah where no one sees him. ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُ بِمَغْفِرَةٍ وأجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ ("so give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward"). The meaning is: "whoever follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful, give him glad tidings of forgiveness and a generous reward". ”اَلْمَغْفِرَةُ“ is the pardoning of his sins, and ”أجْرٍ كَرِيمٍ“ is through Paradise.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي المَوْتى ونَكْتُبُ ما قَدَّمُوا وآثارَهُمْ﴾ ("it is We who give life to the dead, and We record what they have sent ahead and their traces"): what they have put forward of their deeds; and We record their traces, that is: whoever establishes a good practice, its reward is recorded for him, and whoever establishes an evil practice, its punishment is recorded against him. It has also been said: ”وَنَكْتُبُ آثارَهم“, that is: their footsteps. The first is more common and clearer.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
﴿واضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلا﴾ ("and strike for them a parable"). ”مَثَلًا“ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The meaning of people's saying ”اِضْرِبْ لَهُ مَثَلًا“ is: "mention to him a parable". It is said: ”عِنْدِي مِن هَذا الضَّرْبِ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ“ ("I have much of this kind"), that is: of this pattern; and you say: "these things are of one ḍarb", that is: of one pattern. So ”اِضْرِبْ لَهم مَثَلًا“ means: ”مَثِّلْ لَهم مَثَلًا“ ("present to them a likeness").
And His saying: ﴿أصْحابَ القَرْيَةِ﴾ ("the people of the town"), that is: "the story of the people of the town". ﴿إذْ جاءَها المُرْسَلُونَ﴾ ("when the messengers came to it"): it has come in the exegesis that they were the people of Antioch; ʿĪsā sent two [messengers] to them, and they called them liars. He said: ﴿فَعَزَّزْنا بِثالِثٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 14] ("so We reinforced them with a third"); it is read ”فَعَزَزْنا“ with shadda and without [i.e. فَعَزَّزْنا and فَعَزَزْنا]. The meaning of ”فَعَزَّزْنا“ is: We strengthened and reinforced the message with a third, that is: with a third messenger. ﴿فَقالُوا إنّا إلَيْكم مُرْسَلُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 14], up to His saying: ﴿البَلاغُ المُبِينُ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 17]: so the messengers informed them that what was incumbent on them was [only] the conveying [of the message].

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿قالُوا إنّا تَطَيَّرْنا بِكُمْ﴾ ("they said: We augur evil from you"), that is: we take you as an ill omen. ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهُوا لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾ ("if you do not desist we will surely stone you"), that is: we will surely kill you by stoning.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿قالُوا طائِرُكم مَعَكُمْ﴾ ("they said: Your omen is with you"). ”طَيْرُكم مَعَكم“ is also permissible, because one says ”طائِرٌ“ and ”طَيْرٌ“ with one meaning; but I do not know anyone who read ”طَيْرُكم“ here, without the alif. The meaning is: "they said: your ill luck is with you". ﴿أإنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾ ("[is it] because you are reminded?"), that is: "If you are reminded, do you augur evil?!" It is also read: ”أأنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ“, that is: "because you are reminded".

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿وَجاءَ مِن أقْصى المَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعى﴾ ("and there came from the farthest end of the city a man, running"). This was a man who used to worship Allah in a cave in a mountain; when he heard of the messengers he came running — that is, hastening — to them, and said: "Do you want a wage for what you have brought?" The messengers said: "No." This man was called — according to what is related — "Ḥabīb the Carpenter". He turned to his people and said: ﴿يا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوا المُرْسَلِينَ﴾ ﴿اتَّبِعُوا مَن لا يَسْألُكم أجْرًا وهم مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 21], up to His saying: ﴿فاسْمَعُونِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 25]; so he made the messengers witnesses to his faith. Qatāda said: "This is a man who called his people to Allah and gave them sincere counsel, and they killed him for that; they set about stoning him while he was saying: O Allah, guide my people! O Allah, guide my people!" So Allah admitted him to Paradise, and he is alive in it, receiving provision. The meaning is: "when his people tormented him, it was said: Enter Paradise"; and when he beheld it he said: ﴿يا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 26] ﴿بِما غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وجَعَلَنِي مِنَ المُكْرَمِينَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 27] ("would that my people knew how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honoured"), that is: [knew] of my Lord's forgiveness of me; “مِنَ المُكْرَمِينَ”, that is: among those admitted to Paradise. It has also been said: “بِما غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي”, that is: would that they knew the deeds and faith by which my Lord forgave me. And “بِمَ غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي” is permissible, in the sense: "for what thing my Lord forgave me"; and it is possible that “بِما” has this meaning with the alif retained: you say “قَدْ عَلِمْتُ بِما صَنَعْتَ هَذا” and “قَدْ عَلِمْتُ بِمَ صَنَعْتَ هَذا”, that is: "I know by what means you did this"; and dropping the alif in this sense is better.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿وَما أنْـزَلْنا عَلى قَوْمِهِ مِن بَعْدِهِ مِن جُنْدٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ ("and We did not send down upon his people after him any host from heaven"). The meaning is: "We did not send down upon them a host; We did not take revenge with a host for the messenger whom they called a liar".

zajjaj:29-29.t: The meaning of ﴿إنْ كانَتْ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً﴾ ("it was but a single cry") is: "it was nothing but a single cry, nothing but that a single cry was cried at them, so they died, punished by it". It is also read: “إلّا صَيْحَةٌ واحِدَةٌ” [in the nominative]; Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī alone read it so, and it is good in Arabic. [Translator's note: the explanation that follows — "no punishment befell them except a single cry", which takes كانَ as complete with صَيْحَةٌ as its agent — fits the nominative reading, although the source introduces it with "whoever reads it in the accusative"; translated as written.] So whoever reads it in the accusative, the meaning is: "no punishment befell them except a single cry". ﴿فَإذا هم خامِدُونَ﴾ ("and at once they were extinguished"), that is: still; they had died and become like extinguished, lifeless ashes.

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿يا حَسْرَةً عَلى العِبادِ﴾ ("O the anguish for the servants!"). It has also been read: “يا حَسْرَةَ العِبادِ”, without “عَلى”; but I do not at all like reading with anything that differs from the muṣḥaf. This is one of the most difficult questions in the Qurʾān, when someone says: what is the benefit in calling out to anguish, when anguish is among the things that do not answer? The benefit in calling out to it is like the benefit in calling out to anything that does not reason, because the vocative (nidāʾ) is a means of alerting. When you say “يا زَيْدُ” ("O Zayd"), if you have not called him in order to address him with something other than the call, then the speech has no meaning; you only say "O Zayd" to alert him by the call, then you say to him: "you did such-and-such" or "do such-and-such", or whatever you like that has some benefit for him. Do you not see that you say to someone who is facing you: “يا زَيْدُ، ما أحْسَنَ ما صَنَعْتَ!” ("O Zayd, how excellent is what you did!")? If you had said to him: “ما أحْسَنَ ما صَنَعْتَ!”, you would have attained, in conveying the benefit, what you made him understand by it; except that your saying "O Zayd" is more emphatic in speech and more effective in making understood. Likewise, when you say to the one addressed: “أنا أعْجَبُ مِمّا فَعَلْتَ” ("I am amazed at what you did"), you have informed him that you are amazed; but if you said: “واعَجَباهُ مِمّا فَعَلْتَ!” ("O the wonder of what you did!") or “يا عَجَباهُ! أتَفْعَلُ كَذا وكَذا؟!” ("O wonder! Do you do such-and-such?!"), your calling out to wonder would be more effective in conveying the point. The meaning is: "O wonder, come forth, for this is one of your times!" Calling out to wonder is only an alerting, so that the one addressed is firmly made aware of the amazement at his deed. Likewise, when you say: “وَيْلٌ لِزَيْدٍ” or “وَيْلَ زَيْدٍ، لِمَ فَعَلَ كَذا وكَذا؟!” ("woe to Zayd, why did he do such-and-such?!"), it is more effective. And likewise in the Book of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ [Hūd: 72], and likewise: ﴿يا حَسْرَتا عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 56], and likewise: ﴿يا حَسْرَةً عَلى العِبادِ﴾. The meaning in the exegesis is that their mockery of the messengers is an anguish upon them. Ḥasra (anguish) is when a person is overcome, from the intensity of regret, by what has no end after it, until his heart remains exhausted (ḥasīr).

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِنَ القُرُونِ أنَّهم إلَيْهِمْ لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they will not return to them?"), that is: so that they fear that the like of what was hastened for others who were destroyed will be hastened for them in this world, and that, besides that, they will never return to this world. The position of “كَمْ” is accusative, governed by “أهْلَكْنا”, because “كَمْ” is not governed by what precedes it, whether it is declarative (khabar) or interrogative. You say in the declarative: “كَمْ سِرْتُ” ("how [far] I travelled!"), meaning: "I travelled many parasangs"; and “سِرْتُ كَمْ فَرْسَخًا” is not permissible. That is because “كَمْ” in its category is in the position of “رُبَّ”, and its origin is interrogation and vagueness. Just as when you ask and say to the one addressed: “كَمْ فَرْسَخًا سِرْتَ؟” ("how many parasangs did you travel?"), “سِرْتُ كَمْ فَرْسَخًا” is not permissible, because an interrogative is not governed by what precedes it — likewise when “كَمْ” is made declarative, the vagueness remains in it. “أنَّهم” is a badal (substitute) from the meaning of ﴿ألَمْ يَرَوْا كَمْ أهْلَكْنا﴾; the meaning is: "have they not seen, of the generations which We destroyed, that they do not return?" And “إنَّهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ”, with kasra of “إنَّ”, is permissible; its meaning is resumption (istiʾnāf); the meaning is: "they will not return to them".

zajjaj:32-32.t: And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنْ كُلٌّ لَمّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("and all of them will surely be brought before Us together"). Whoever reads with the light form, “لَما”, then “ما” is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic, and the meaning is: “إنْ كُلٌّ لَجَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ” ("all, indeed, will be brought before Us together"); its meaning is: "all are nothing but brought before Us together". It is also read “لَمّا” with shadda, and the meaning of “لَمّا” here is “ألّا” [i.e. إلّا, "except"]; you say: “سَألْتُكَ لَمّا فَعَلْتَ” ("I ask you [nothing] but that you do it"). The interpretation of the verse is that they will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and made to stand before what they did.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ الأرْضُ المَيْتَةُ أحْيَيْناها﴾ ("and a sign for them is the dead earth: We gave it life"). It is also read with shadda. The original of “اَلْمَيْتَةُ” is “اَلْمَيِّتَةُ”; the original is with shadda, and the light form is more common, and both are permissible. “آيَةٌ” is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is “لَهم”, that is: "and a sign for them, indicating to them the oneness of Allah and that Allah raises the dead, is the giving of life to the dead earth". It is also possible that “آيَةٌ” is nominative as mubtadaʾ and its khabar is “اَلْأرْضُ المَيْتَةُ”.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿وَفَجَّرْنا فِيها مِنَ العُيُونِ﴾ ﴿لِيَأْكُلُوا مِن ثَمَرِهِ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 35] ("and We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they may eat of its fruit"). “ثُمْرِهِ” is also permissible, with sukūn on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ. ﴿وَما عَمِلَتْهُ أيْدِيهِمْ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 35] ("and what their hands have made"): it is also read “عَمِلَتْ” without the hāʾ. The position of “ما” is genitive; the meaning is: "that they may eat of its fruit and of what their hands have made". It is also possible that “ما” is a negation, in the sense: "that they may eat of its fruit, while their hands did not make it" — this is with the hāʾ retained. When the hāʾ is dropped, the preferred analysis is that “ما” is in the position of a genitive and that “ما” is in the sense of “اَلَّذِي” ("that which"), so dropping the hāʾ is good; and this would be in line with His saying: ﴿أفَرَأيْتُمْ ما تَحْرُثُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 63] ﴿أأنْتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُ أمْ نَحْنُ الزّارِعُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 64].

zajjaj:36-36.t: And His saying: ﴿سُبْحانَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الأزْواجَ كُلَّها﴾ ("glory be to Him who created all the pairs"). “سُبْحانَ” is declaring Allah free of every evil and exalting Him above it. The meaning of “اَلْأزْواجُ” is all the kinds — of plants, animals and others. ﴿وَمِن أنْفُسِهِمْ ومِمّا لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("and of themselves and of what they do not know"): of what Allah has created of all the species and likenesses.

zajjaj:37-37.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ اللَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنهُ النَّهارَ﴾ ("and a sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it"). The meaning of “نَسْلَخُ” is: We bring the day out of it in such a way that nothing of the light of day remains with it; and that is among the signs that indicate the oneness of Allah and His power.

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿والشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَها﴾ ("and the sun runs to a resting place of its own"). The meaning is: "and a sign for them is the sun, running to a resting place of its own", that is: to a term that has been appointed for it and decreed for it. Whoever reads: “لا مُسْتَقَرَّ لَها” ("it has no resting place"), its meaning is that it runs forever and does not stay fixed in any place.

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿والقَمَرَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ﴾ ("and the moon — We have determined for it phases"). It is read with the nominative and the accusative. Whoever reads the accusative takes it as: “وَقَدَّرْنا القَمَرَ مَنازِلَ قَدَّرْناهُ مَنازِلَ”; and the nominative is in the sense: “وَآيَةٌ لَهُمُ القَمَرُ قَدَّرْناهُ” ("and a sign for them is the moon: We have determined it"); it is also possible that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and “قَدَّرْناهُ” the khabar (predicate). ﴿حَتّى عادَ كالعُرْجُونِ القَدِيمِ﴾ ("until it returns like an old date-stalk"). “اَلْعُرْجُونُ” is the stalk of the date-cluster which is called “اَلْكِباسَةُ”; the true sense of al-ʿurjūn is that it is the stalk on which the cluster hangs. “اَلْعُرْجُونُ” is the stalk of the cluster on which the sprigs of the cluster sit; when it dries and becomes old it becomes thin and small, and then it resembles the crescent moon at the end of the month and at its first rising. The pattern of “عُرْجُونٌ” is “فُعْلُولٌ”, from “اَلِانْعِراجُ” (bending).

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿لا الشَّمْسُ يَنْبَغِي لَها أنْ تُدْرِكَ القَمَرَ﴾ ("it is not for the sun to overtake the moon") — the verse. The meaning is: "neither of them takes away the meaning of the other". ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ ("and each is swimming in an orbit"): each one of them has an orbit. The meaning of “يَسْبَحُونَ” is: they travel in it with ease and expansiveness; and everyone who moves freely in something has "swum" in it; and from that is swimming in water.

zajjaj:41-41.t: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَهم أنّا حَمَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهم في الفُلْكِ المَشْحُونِ﴾ ("and a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship"). The people of Mecca were addressed with this. It was said “حَمَلْنا ذُرِّيَّتَهم” ("We carried their offspring") because those who were carried with Noah — peace be upon him — in the ship are their forefathers, and their [descendants are their] offspring. “اَلْمَشْحُونُ” in the language means: filled. “شَحَنْتُ السَّفِينَةَ” — when I have filled it; and “شَحَنْتُ المَدِينَةَ” and “أشْحَنْتُها” — when I have filled it.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying: ﴿وَخَلَقْنا لَهم مِن مِثْلِهِ ما يَرْكَبُونَ﴾ ("and We created for them the like of it, which they ride"). The majority in the exegesis is that “مِن مِثْلِهِ” means: of the like of Noah's ship. It has also been said that by “مِن مِثْلِهِ” He means the camels, and that camels in the desert are in the position of ships at sea.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
﴿وَإنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهم فَلا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We could drown them, and there would be no one to answer their cry"), that is: there would be no helper for them.
﴿إلا رَحْمَةً مِنّا﴾ [Yā Sīn: 44] ("except as a mercy from Us") is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "they are not rescued except out of a mercy from Us and for enjoyment until a time — until the expiry of the appointed term".

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّقُوا ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيكم وما خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ ("and when it is said to them: Beware of what is before you and what is behind you"): what you have committed in the past of your sins, and what you will do in what lies ahead of you. It has also been said: “ما بَيْنَ أيْدِيكم وما خَلْفَكم” in the sense: "beware lest there descend upon you of punishment the like of what descended upon the nations before you"; “وَما خَلْفَكم”, that is: "beware of the punishment of the Hereafter". Similar to it is: ﴿فَإنْ أعْرَضُوا فَقُلْ أنْذَرْتُكم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 13].

zajjaj:47-47.t: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم أنْفِقُوا مِمّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ ("and when it is said to them: Spend of what Allah has provided you"), that is: "feed [others] and give charity". ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنُطْعِمُ مَن لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ أطْعَمَهُ﴾ ("those who disbelieve say to those who believe: Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would have fed?"): it is as though they say this by way of mockery. It has come in the exegesis that it was revealed concerning the zanādiqa (freethinkers), and it has been said: concerning a group of the Jews.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هَذا الوَعْدُ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ ("and they say: When is this promise, if you are truthful?"): "When will this promise be fulfilled? Show it to us."

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿ما يَنْظُرُونَ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهم وهم يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾ ("they await nothing but a single cry which will seize them while they are disputing"). In “يَخِصِّمُونَ” there are four ways. [First,] sukūn of the khāʾ and the ṣād, with shadda on the ṣād, combining two quiescent letters; this is the harshest and worst of the four. One of those who transmit the reading of the people of Medina used to hold that this was not accurately recorded from the people of Medina, just as “إلى بارِئْكم” was not accurately recorded from Abū ʿAmr; he held that in this the vowel — the fatḥa of the khāʾ — is only slurred (ikhtilās), and the matter is as he said. The good reading is “يَخَصِّمُونَ”, with fatḥa on the khāʾ; the original is “يَخْتَصِمُونَ”: the fatḥa of the tāʾ was cast onto the khāʾ, and [the tāʾ] was assimilated into the ṣād. Kasra on the khāʾ is also good: the khāʾ is given a kasra because of its being quiescent along with the quiescence of the ṣād. It has also been read “يَخْتَصِمُونَ”, and that too is good. Its meaning is: "it seizes them while some of them dispute with others". It is also possible [that it means]: "it seizes them while they, among themselves, are disputing about the argument that they will not be raised; so the Hour comes while they are busy with their affairs".

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً﴾ ("then they will not be able to make a bequest"): no one will be able to give instructions about any of his affairs. ﴿وَلا إلى أهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("nor will they return to their families"): he will not remain [alive] until he gets to his family and his home; he dies in his place.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَنُفِخَ في الصُّورِ فَإذا هم مِنَ الأجْداثِ إلى رَبِّهِمْ يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ ("and the trumpet will be blown, and at once from the graves they will hasten to their Lord"). “اَلصُّورُ”, as has come in the exegesis, is the horn into which Isrāfīl will blow. Abū ʿUbayda said that “اَلصُّورُ” is the plural of “صُورَةٌ” (form); but [the plural of] “صُورَةٌ” is “صُوَرٌ”, as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَصَوَّرَكم فَأحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 3], and no one read “أحْسَنَ صُورَكم”, nor did anyone read “وَنُفِخَ في الصُّوَرِ” by any established route. “اَلْأجْداثُ” are the graves; its singular is “جَدَثٌ”. “يَنْسِلُونَ” means: they come out quickly.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالُوا يا ويْلَنا مَن بَعَثَنا مِن مَرْقَدِنا﴾ ("they will say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping place?"): this is the complete stop (waqf al-tamām), and this is the saying of the polytheists.
And His saying: ﴿هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وصَدَقَ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾ ("this is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth"). “هَذا” is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is “ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ”; and this is the saying of the polytheists — I mean “هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ”. It is also possible that “هَذا” is a naʿt (adjective) of “مَرْقَدِنا”, in the sense: "Who has raised us from this sleeping place of ours in which we were sleeping?" Then “ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ وصَدَقَ المُرْسَلُونَ” is on two accounts: one of them with “هَذا” implied, and the second with “حَقٌّ” ("true") implied, so that the meaning is: "true is what the Most Merciful promised". The first view — I mean that “هَذا” begins a new sentence — is what the exegesis holds, and it is the view of the philologists. [Translator's note: the source attributes «هَذا ما وعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ» to the polytheists in both places; translated as written.]

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿إنْ كانَتْ إلا صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً﴾ ("it will be but a single cry"), and “إلّا صَيْحَةٌ واحِدَةٌ”; their i'rab has already been discussed. ﴿فَإذا هم جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("and at once they will all be brought before Us"). So the meaning is: "their destruction was by a cry, and their raising and revival is by a cry".

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿فاليَوْمَ لا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا ولا تُجْزَوْنَ إلا ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("so today no soul will be wronged in anything, and you will be recompensed only for what you used to do"). The meaning is: "whoever is recompensed is recompensed only according to his deeds".

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿إنَّ أصْحابَ الجَنَّةِ اليَوْمَ في شُغُلٍ فاكِهُونَ﴾ ("the people of Paradise today are busy in enjoyment"). The interpretation of “فاكِهُونَ” is “فَرِحُونَ” ("joyful"). It has come in the exegesis that their occupation is deflowering virgins; and it has been said: "occupied [and away] from what the people of the Fire are in". It is read “في شُغُلٍ” and “شُغْلٍ”; and “شُغْلٌ” and “شُغُلٌ” are permissible in Arabic.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿هم وأزْواجُهم في ظِلالٍ﴾ ("they and their spouses, in shades"), and “ظُلَلٍ”; “ظُلُلٍ” is also permissible.
﴿عَلى الأرائِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾ ("reclining on couches"): these are the bedding-spreads in curtained canopies (ḥijāl). It has been said that they are the spreads, and it has been said: “اَلْأسِرَّةُ” ("the beds"). In reality they are “اَلْفُرُشُ” ("spreads"), whether in canopies or not in canopies.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿لَهم فِيها فاكِهَةٌ ولَهم ما يَدَّعُونَ﴾ ("they will have fruit therein, and they will have whatever they call for"), that is: whatever they wish for. It is said: “فُلانٌ في خَيْرِ ما ادَّعى” ("so-and-so is in the best of what he claimed"), that is: "what he wished for". It is taken from “اَلدُّعاءُ” (calling, supplication); the meaning is: "everything the people of Paradise call for comes to them".

zajjaj:58-58.t: ﴿سَلامٌ قَوْلا مِن رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾ ("Peace — a word from a Merciful Lord"). “سَلامٌ” is a badal (substitute) for “ما”; the meaning is: "they will have what they wish for: peace", that is: "and this is the wish of the people of Paradise — that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, should greet them with peace". “قَوْلًا” is accusative in the sense: "they will have peace, which Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — says as a word".

zajjaj:59-59.t: ﴿وامْتازُوا اليَوْمَ أيُّها المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ ("and stand apart today, O criminals"), that is: separate yourselves from the believers.

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿ألَمْ أعْهَدْ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ ("did I not enjoin upon you"). It is also read “أعْهِدْ” with kasra, and the fatḥa is more common, according to your saying “عَهِدَ، يَعْهَدُ”. The kasra is permissible on two accounts: on [the pattern] “عَهَدَ، يَعْهِدُ”, and on “عَهِدَ، يَعْهِدُ”, like “حَسِبَ، يَحْسِبُ”. Its meaning is: "Did I not lay upon you beforehand the covenant of faith and of abandoning the worship of Satan?"

zajjaj:62-62.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ أضَلَّ مِنكم جِبِلا﴾ ("and he has led astray a great multitude of you"). It is also read “جِبِلًّا”, with kasra on the jīm and the bāʾ, and it is read “جُبُلًا”, with ḍamma on the jīm and the bāʾ.
