And it is read “جُبْلًا”, with sukūn on the bāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm. “جَبْلًا”, with fatḥa on the jīm, and “جِبْلًا”, with kasra on the jīm, are permissible; and “جِبَلًا”, with kasra on the jīm and fatḥa on the bāʾ, without shadda on the lām, is also permissible, as the plural of “جِبْلَةٌ” — [so] “جِبَلٌ”. “اَلْجِبْلَةُ”, in all of that, means: a great creation and many created beings.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَطَمَسْنا عَلى أعْيُنِهِمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We would have obliterated their eyes"). “اَلْمَطْمُوسُ” is the blind person whose eyelid cannot be distinguished, the edge of whose eye cannot be seen. That is: "if We willed We would have blinded them, so they would have strayed from the path — so how would they see if We did that to them?"

zajjaj:67-67.t: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَمَسَخْناهم عَلى مَكانَتِهِمْ﴾ ("and if We willed We would have transformed them in their places"), and “وَمَكاناتِهِمْ”; “اَلْمَكانَةُ” and “اَلْمَكانُ” have one meaning. ﴿فَما اسْتَطاعُوا مُضِيًّا ولا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ ("so they could neither go on nor turn back"), that is: they would be able neither to go nor to come.

zajjaj:68-68.t: ﴿وَمَن نُعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّسْهُ﴾ ("and whomever We grant long life, We reverse him [in creation]"), and “نَنْكُسْهُ” and “نَنْكِسْهُ”; one says: “نَكَسْتُهُ، أنْكُسُهُ، وأنْكِسُهُ” — all of them. Its meaning is: "whomever We give a long life, We reverse his constitution", so that in place of strength there is weakness, and in place of youth decrepitude.

zajjaj:69-69.t: ﴿وَما عَلَّمْناهُ الشِّعْرَ وما يَنْبَغِي لَهُ﴾ ("and We did not teach him poetry, nor is it fitting for him"), that is: We did not teach Muḥammad ﷺ the composing of poetry, nor is it fitting for him, that is: it does not come easily to him. ﴿إنْ هو إلا ذِكْرٌ وقُرْآنٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ("it is only a Reminder and a clear Qurʾān"), that is: what the Prophet ﷺ brought, which the unbelievers claimed is poetry, is not poetry. This does not entail that the Prophet ﷺ never once quoted a verse of poetry; it only entails that the Prophet — peace be upon him — is not a poet, and that the Qurʾān which he brought is from Allah, because it is distinct from the speech of created beings and from the metres of the poetry of the Arabs. The Qurʾān is an inimitable sign, indicating that the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ and his signs are established forever.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ مَن كانَ حَيًّا﴾ ("that he may warn whoever is alive"). It is possible that the implied pronoun in His saying “لِيُنْذِرَ” is the Prophet — peace be upon him — and it is possible that it is the Qurʾān. The meaning of “مَن كانَ حَيًّا” is: whoever understands what he is addressed with; for the unbeliever is like the dead in that he has not reflected so as to know that the Prophet ﷺ and what he brought are true. ﴿وَيَحِقَّ القَوْلُ عَلى الكافِرِينَ﴾ ("and that the word may come true against the unbelievers"); “وَيَحُقَّ القَوْلُ” is also permissible, that is: the proof is established against them. “لِتُنْذِرَ مَن كانَ حَيًّا”, with the tāʾ, is also permissible, as "an address to the Prophet ﷺ"; and “لِيَنْذَرَ”, that is: "that he may know", is permissible; one says: “نَذِرْتُ بِكَذا وكَذا، أنْذَرُ” ("I became aware of such-and-such"), like “عَلِمْتُ، أعْلَمُ”.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَهم لَها مالِكُونَ﴾ ("so they are its owners"): the meaning of “مالِكُونَ” is: in control [of them], because the intent here is that they are made submissive to them. Do you not see His saying: “وَذَلَّلْناها لَهم” ("and We have subdued them for them")? Similar to it in poetry:
؎أصْبَحْتُ لا أحْمِلُ السِّلاحَ ولا ∗∗∗ أمْلِكُ رَأْسَ البَعِيرِ إنْ نَفَرا
(I have come to be one who no longer bears arms, nor can I control the camel's head if it bolts.)
That is: I cannot control the camel's head.

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying: ﴿فَمِنها رَكُوبُهُمْ﴾ ("and of them are their mounts"): its meaning is: "what they ride"; and the evidence is the reading of whoever read: “فَمِنها رَكُوبَتُهم”. “رُكُوبُهم”, with ḍamma on the rāʾ, is also permissible, though I do not know anyone who read it so, in the sense: "of them is their riding, their eating and their drinking".

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿وَهم لَهم جُنْدٌ مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ ("while they are for them a host brought forth"), that is: they [the worshippers] rally to the support of the idols, while the idols are unable to help them.

zajjaj:78-78.t: And His saying: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ﴾ ("and he strikes for Us a parable and forgets his own creation") — the verse. It has come in the exegesis that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Prophet ﷺ with a decayed bone, crumbled it, then scattered it and said: "Who will give life to this?" So the answer to him was: ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79] ("say: He will give them life who produced them the first time"); for power in originating is clearer than in restoring. It is said that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was the one in the story, and it is said: al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.

zajjaj:81-81.t: And He informed them that the creation of the heavens and the earth is more far-reaching in power, and [that He has power] over reviving the dead; so He said: ﴿أوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ﴾ ("is not He who created the heavens and the earth…") — the verse. And He said in another place: ﴿لَخَلْقُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ أكْبَرُ مِن خَلْقِ النّاسِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 57].

zajjaj:83-83.t: And He said: ﴿فَسُبْحانَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ ("so glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things"): its meaning is declaring Allah free of every evil and of being described as anything other than powerful. ﴿الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾, that is: power over everything. ﴿وَإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("and to Him you will be returned"), and “تَرْجِعُونَ” ("you will return"), that is: He will raise you after your death.
